Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verses 1–2:

الحمدللہ الذی لہ ۔۔۔۔۔ وھو الرحیم الغفور (1 – 2) ” ۔ “۔

This is the opening of the surah, in which the discussion concerns the polytheism of the idolaters, their denial of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), their doubts about the Hereafter, and their regarding the resurrection after death as impossible. The opening is with the words that all praise is for Allah, who is Praiseworthy in Himself even if none of His creatures praises Him. He is praiseworthy throughout this entire universe, and all the forces and creatures of this universe praise Allah, even if these humans do not praise Him.

Along with praise, there is mention of this attribute of Allah: that Allah is the Owner of the heavens and the earth. No one has any right over Allah. Neither in the earth nor in the heavens is there any partner with Allah. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, and this is the first and foundational point of the Islamic worldview. The Owner of this vast and wide universe is Allah, and there is no partner besides Him.

ولہ الحمد فی الاخرۃ (34: 1) “And to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter.” That is, Allah is praiseworthy in His own Essence, and the praise offered by the servants is also for Him. In short, the praise of those who deny Allah or associate others with Him is also for Allah alone; He alone deserves it, and this will be made manifest to them in the Hereafter.

وھو الحکیم الخبیر (34: 1) “And He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.” He is such a Wise One that none of His acts is devoid of wisdom. He also manages the earth and the heavens with wisdom. He administers this universe with the utmost wisdom. He is aware of everything; He has knowledge of every matter, and His knowledge is very deep, comprehensive and all-encompassing. If you wish to see the knowledge of Allah, then for an example look at one page of His Book of knowledge.

یعلم ما یلج ۔۔۔۔۔ یعرج فیھا (34: 2) “He knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, what descends from the heaven and what ascends into it.” These are a few words; reflect upon them. How many things enter the earth, how many come out of it, how many descend from the heavens, and how many ascend, in various movements, various forms, various shapes, various conceptions and various manifestations. They are so many that imagination cannot contain them within its sphere. If all the people of the earth were to try to count the aforementioned actions occurring in a single second, they would be unable to count them, even if they spent their entire lives at this task. Certainly they could not do it, because countless things enter and exit the earth in that single moment, and countless things descend and ascend from the heavens. How many seeds fall into the earth and how many shoots emerge, how many insects enter and exit, how many celestial bodies and creatures, how many drops of water, how many particles of gas, and how many particles of mist enter the surroundings of the earth, and how many other things enter and leave. The eye of Allah sees them and counts them.

Just look at plants! Look at springs, look at volcanic mountains, look at other gases, and see how many hidden treasures there are; and look at the creeping creatures which are visible and those which cannot be seen even by microscopes. Man has gained knowledge about some of them, and countless others are still unknown.

Can you count the drops of rain descending from the heavens? Meteorites are not drops, yet their number is known. At any moment, rays emerge from the sun: how many burning rays, how many light-giving rays, how many decrees are being executed, and how many remain hidden. How many mercies are upon the common people and how many are destined to fall upon some servants. How much provision is distributed and how much provision is withheld, and what there is that is known only to Allah's knowledge.

How many souls and how many breaths ascend towards the heavens: of plants, of animals, of germs, and of other creatures; and how many calls are being given by Allah, openly or secretly, which no one hears except Allah! How many souls there are that we know or do not know. They ascend to Allah, and how many angels return every day to Allah, and how many souls there are in this universe that only Allah knows.

How many particles of vapour and other gas particles rise from the sea, whose knowledge is with Allah alone. All these things perform their action in a single moment. This is a matter of one moment, the counting of which all humans cannot accomplish even by spending their entire lives, even if they were to spend their ages, whereas the knowledge of Allah is all-encompassing and comprehensive. The accounting of these events, in every moment, every era and every place, is with Him; rather, He reckons even the movements, stillnesses, thoughts and whisperings of man. Yet He is Concealing (Sattar) and conceals the weaknesses of man.

وھو الرحیم الغفور (34: 2) “And He is the Most Merciful, the Most Forgiving.”

Each one of these verses of the Qur'an indicates that this Qur'an is not human speech. The nature of human intellect is such that it cannot even present a conception so profound that it cannot leap to its limits. Such general and comprehensive ideas cannot arise in the human imagination. And such comprehensive knowledge, containing meanings and implications whose encompassing is impossible, does not exist in human speech, because human speech is the product of human intellect, and this is contrary to the nature of human intellect. Verses of this kind differ from the speech of servants.

After the proof of the comprehensiveness of Allah's knowledge and the all-encompassing and miraculous expression, it is stated that the people of disbelief deny the Resurrection, while their own knowledge is so limited that they do not know what will happen tomorrow. Whereas Allah is All-Knowing and All-Seeing. Nothing in the heavens and the earth is beyond His knowledge, and the Resurrection is necessary so that both the righteous and the wicked receive the consequences of their deeds.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verses 3–5:

وقال الذین کفروا ۔۔۔۔۔۔ من رجز الیم (3 – 5)

The denial of the Hereafter by the disbelievers was due to their failure to comprehend the wisdom of Allah contained in the creation of mankind and the divine destiny. The wisdom of Allah requires that people not be left like unbridled camels, such that whoever does good has his own choice and whoever does evil has his own choice. Neither should the doer of good be rewarded nor the evildoer be punished. Through His Messengers, Allah had warned people that a portion of the reward remains for the Hereafter, and a portion of the punishment is also reserved for the Hereafter. Therefore, those whose understanding of the wisdom of creation is complete know that for the fulfilment of Allah's plan it is necessary that the Hereafter be established, so that Allah's promise is fulfilled and Allah's announcement is proved true. It is only this wisdom that remains hidden from the sight of the disbelievers. For this reason they used to say:

لا تاتینا الساعۃ (34: 3) "The Hour will not come upon us." And Allah strongly refutes their statement:

قل بلی وربی لتاتینکم (34: 3) "Say: Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come upon you." Allah is true, and His Messengers are also true. They do not know the unseen, but they rely upon Allah and have certainty. In matters of which they themselves have no knowledge, they put their trust in Allah. Allah, who emphatically declares that the Hour will come, is the Knower of the unseen, so His word is true because it is based upon knowledge.

Now the knowledge of Allah is presented in the form of a cosmic reality, just as at the very beginning of the Surah a comprehensive example of it was given. That testimony showed that this Qur'an is not human speech, because comprehensive parables of this kind cannot be the product of human thought. Now read the same point here in other words.

لا یعزب عنہ مثقال۔۔۔۔ فی کتب مبین (34: 3) "Not an atom's weight in the heavens or in the earth escapes Him; nor is there anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear Book." I repeat here that this concept is not a human concept, nor does man think in such comprehensive terms. Among all the specimens of human speech to date, whether in verse or in prose, such comprehensive a statement is not found. Whenever man presents a view about the comprehensiveness of knowledge and its encompassing, it is not so cosmic in colour.

لا یعزب عنہ ۔۔۔۔۔ من ذلک ولا اکبر (34: 3) "Not an atom's weight in the heavens or in the earth escapes Him, nor is there anything smaller than that or greater." In the specimens of human speech, at least, there is not found for the inclusion, depth and comprehensiveness of knowledge a style such as the Qur'an has adopted. It is Allah alone who can describe the comprehensiveness of His knowledge in this manner, and describe the depth of His knowledge. These matters cannot come within the scope of human imagination. Likewise, the concept of the Divinity among Muslims rises to a height whose example does not come to their minds. They worship Him while understanding their concept and imagination, and considering it beyond imagination and beyond conception.

The question is: what is the Clear Book? The Clear Book is none other than the knowledge of Allah, which has encompassed everything. Nothing escapes from it, not even the particle that moves within the universe, neither smaller than an atom nor greater than it.

Consider this expression carefully: "nor smaller than an atom." Until the time of the revelation of the Qur'an, the well-known and famous belief was that the atom was the smallest body; a notion of anything smaller did not exist. Today, by splitting the atom, man has come to know that there is something smaller than the atom. At that time it had no existence in human thought or calculation. Blessed is Allah, that His servants know those secrets and mysteries of His attributes too. Other people accept them centuries later, and it is Allah who, whenever He wills, lifts the veil from those secrets and mysteries. Why will this Hour be established? Of which the final and complete knowledge belongs to Allah, who knows the small and the great?

لیجزی الذین امنوا ۔۔۔۔۔۔ من رجز الیم (34: 4 – 5) "And this Hour will come so that Allah may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds. For them is forgiveness and an honourable provision. And for those who strove to frustrate Our verses, there is a painful punishment of the most evil kind."

This is the wisdom of Allah, His will and His arrangement. Allah has decreed that He will fully reward those who did righteous deeds after believing, and will also punish those who strove with all their effort to frustrate Allah's verses. Those who believed, and whose faith appeared in the form of righteous deeds, for them is forgiveness, for those matters which went wrong for them and for the shortcomings that occurred, and then after forgiveness, for them is an honourable provision. The word "provision" occurs often in this Surah; what is meant is Paradise, because the blessings of Allah are an honourable provision.

As for those who made efforts to frustrate Allah's verses and exerted their full strength against the Islamic movement, for them is a painful punishment. "Rijz" is the term used for an extremely evil punishment. This is because they opposed the Islamic movement, strove to defeat the movement, and kept struggling on an evil path. Thus Allah's wisdom and His plan are completed, and the view that these people have adopted, that the Hereafter will not be established, is due to their ignorance. Whereas people of knowledge know that it will certainly come.

Those people became convinced that the Hour would not come, although it is one of the unseen matters specific to Allah, and Allah has decided that it will surely come. Allah alone is the Knower of the unseen. He commanded the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to proclaim this message, and that their belief is founded upon ignorance. People of knowledge too have reached the conclusion that the believers have reached. This is the path of Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 34, verse 6:

﴿Those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.﴾ (34:6)

Some narrations state that "those who have been given knowledge" refers to the People of the Book, who, through the prophecies in their own scriptures, knew that the Qur'an is a book of truth and that it guides to the Straight Path. However, the scope of this verse is not limited to the People of the Book. It refers to people of knowledge in general. This verse is not confined to any particular time or place. The people of knowledge of every era fall within its scope; people of every age, every generation and every kind of knowledge are meant, provided that their knowledge is sound knowledge. For the Noble Qur'an is an open book for all times. The truth within it is the truth for the people of knowledge of every era and every region. This book contains the very truth that lies at the heart of this universe. Therefore, the Noble Qur'an is the best and most truthful translation of this cosmic truth.

﴿And it guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾ (34:6). The path of Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, is that which Allah has chosen for this universe, and the same path Allah has chosen for man too, so that human conduct harmonizes with the universe in which man lives. This path is the law of nature and the path of the order of creation, according to which this universe moves, and according to which human life itself moves, because human life, in its system and its pace, is not separate from this universe, nor separate from all the things that exist in it.

It guides to the path of Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, in that it creates in the perceptive faculty of the believers a balanced conception of the universe, and then creates a conception of the believers' relations, connections and values with the universe: what the station of man is within the universe, what the role of man is within it, how man and the universe spread around him can together bring into action the wisdom of Allah's creation, and how man and this universe together can journey towards the direction of Allah, glorified is His majesty.

This truth guides man to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, in that it gives man a method of thought. It raises this thinking upon extremely firm foundations, and these cosmic influences, acting upon the human nature, grant him the best perception of this universe. Man comprehends the properties and laws of this universe and benefits from them. Then, instead of colliding with cosmic realities, he comes into harmony with them.

This truth shows man the way of Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, in that it trains the individual and teaches him to move in harmony with a society. Then it brings one society into harmony with other societies for the construction and progress of this entire universe, and it makes all societies move in step with this universe, so that this universe and the human societies within it may proceed with great ease.

This truth also guides towards the path of Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, in that it gives man and human society laws that are in harmony with human nature. It gives such directives concerning human life and human livelihood that man walks in harmony with all living creatures. Let it not be that the human system is in conflict with the system of this universe and the other animals within it, although man too is one community among the creatures and communities of this earth.

In short, this Book and this truth are a guide to the straight path, and this guide too is sent down by Allah, and this path too is created by Him. If you have to travel along a road, and you find as your guide the very engineer who drew the plan of that road, how fortunate are you, and with what grace and carefree ease will you be able to complete that journey? Certainly, with great tranquility!

After this sensitive commentary, the discussion now returns to the subject of resurrection after death. It is remarked with astonishment how greatly these people raise objections to resurrection after death. From their own side, they marvel at the Prophet (ﷺ), that he speaks such unlikely things, or that he fabricates lies against Allah, whereas their own astonishment is foolish.

This is the commentary of Sayyid Qutb in *Fi Zilal al-Quran* (Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verses 7–8:

﴿And those who disbelieve say...﴾ to ﴿...and far error﴾ (7–8)

These people found the Day of Resurrection so strange. They regarded the one who spoke of it as either a marvel, a madman, or a small-minded person. Look at the way they speak: ﴿Shall we show you a man who tells you that when you are completely torn apart, you will be created anew?﴾ A strange and wondrous person has appeared who says such unthinkable things: that after death, after you have become particles of dust, and after you have mingled with the soil, you will be brought back to life.

These people go further in their wonder. Regarding it as utterly unprecedented, they spread the propaganda that either this man fabricates lies against God, or that he is mad. In their assumption, such statements can only be made by either a liar or a madman. If he is mad, then this speech is raving; and if he is a liar, then it is astonishing. Why do they say these things? Because the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) says that you will be created again, yet his own claim seems astonishing to them. Were these people not created the first time? Is the creation of a human being a small matter? Creation for the first time? If they looked at this with reflection and contemplation, they would never be astonished. But they are misguided and do not take the path of guidance. For this reason, they are severely threatened for this astonishment of theirs.

﴿But those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in torment and far error﴾ (34:8). ﴿Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in torment and in far error.﴾ The "torment" here may also refer to the torment of the Hereafter, as if that torment has already befallen them. Since they have gone very far into error, there is now no hope of their coming to guidance. It may also have another meaning: that just as these people are afflicted by the punishment of God, they are likewise astray. This is a very profound truth, because a person who has no ideology is, psychologically, in severe torment and conflict. Such a person, amid the injustices of the world, has no hope of justice, nor of recompense in the Hereafter, nor of reward in the afterlife. In human life there come events and calamities that a person can endure only for the sake of the reward of the Hereafter, and he is consoled by the knowledge that for the good-doer there is a good reward, and for the wrongdoer there is punishment. There are many hardships that a person endures for the sake of God's pleasure and the reward of the Hereafter, because in the Hereafter not even the smallest deed is lost. Even if it is the weight of an atom and is inside a rock, God brings forth that required particle, even if it is the size of a mustard seed. Whoever is deprived of this fresh, joyful, and bright lamp is, in effect, in everlasting punishment. In this world too, a denier of the Hereafter is caught in continuous torment, and in the Hereafter he will certainly receive the recompense for his deeds. The truth is that belief in the Hereafter is a mercy for mankind and a great blessing, deserved by the sincere servants of God, who continually reflect upon the truth and whose constant desire is to remain on the straight path. The more accepted view is that this verse points to this very point: that those who do not believe in the Hereafter, along with their error, are also caught in a calamity in this world.

Now these deniers are given a severe warning: that if God wills, He may send further worldly punishment upon them because of their misguidance, may cause a piece of the sky to fall upon them, or may cause them to sink into the earth because of this misguidance. They do not reflect upon this order of the cosmos, which could fall into disorder at any moment.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verse 9:

﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and behind them of the heaven and the earth?﴾ ... ﴿Surely in that is a sign for every servant who turns back in repentance.﴾

This is a terrifying cosmic scene. This scene is drawn from their observations, which they witness night and day. The sinking of the earth is also a human observation, and it is mentioned in stories and reports. Likewise, falling meteors and falling lightning bolts are heavenly objects that have been falling. All these things are seen and heard by them. By drawing their attention to such frightening conditions, they are warned, those who deny the Resurrection. If Allah wished to punish them before the Day of Resurrection, it would not be a difficult matter. In this very earth and this very sky, that punishment could be given to them, which surrounds them from before and behind, and which is not far from them, just as the Resurrection appears distant to them. The truth is that only heedless people feel secure from the punishment of Allah.

These are the phenomena they observe within the heavens: lightning, meteors, the sinking of the earth, and earthquakes. At any time, if any of these punishments were to come upon them, it would be a Resurrection in itself.

﴿Surely in that is a sign for every servant who turns back in repentance﴾ (34:9). The truth is that in this there is a sign for every servant who turns back to God, and for one who has not gone so far down the wrong path.

Lesson No. 195 – At a Glance

This lesson presents two forms of gratitude and rebellion, and gives the example that Allah subjects to His special servants forces that are generally not subjected to people. However, the will of Allah and His decree cannot be made subject to people's habits. Among these outlines, the reality of the jinn also comes to light, those whom some Arabs used to worship, or from whom these Arab tribes sought news of the unseen, whereas the jinn themselves are deprived of news of the unseen. In this lesson, the causes of misguidance by which Satan leads people astray are also explained, but these causes lie within the scope of human choice. It is also shown that Allah brings to light the deeds of people that are hidden, and the lesson concludes, as the previous one did, with a mention of the Hereafter.

Lesson No. 195 – Explanation of the Verses

Verses 10 to 21

Laqad atayna Dawooda minna... inni bima ta'maluna baseer (10–11): "And with the instruction: make coats of mail and measure well their links. And act righteously; indeed I am Seeing of what you do." Dawud (Dawud, peace be upon him) was an obedient servant of Allah. The previous lesson ended with this mention.

Inna fi dhalika la-ayatan li-kulli 'abdin muneeb: "Indeed in that is a sign for every servant who turns back (to Allah)." After this indication, the story of Dawud was brought, and it began with that which was given to him as a virtue.

Ya jibalu awwibi ma'ahu wal-tayr (34:10): "O mountains, echo with him, and O birds, (do so) too." It is reported in the narrations that Dawud (peace be upon him) was given a very beautiful voice. This voice, in its beauty, was a miraculous voice. He would sing his hymns with great melodiousness. These hymns were full of the praise of Allah. Some of them are still extant, although we cannot say anything about their authenticity. It is reported in a hadith that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard the voice of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who used to recite the Qur'an at night, and he stood listening. He (ﷺ) said that he had been given a melodious voice in the same way as Dawud (peace be upon him) had been given.

In this verse, the picture drawn of Allah's grace upon Dawud (peace be upon him) is so clear that, as a result of his praise and glorification, the veils between him and this universe were lifted. The reality of him became harmonious with the reality of the universe. And just as he sang the praise of the Lord, the distances between his existence and the reality of the universe vanished. This universe was also a singer of praises to Allah, and so was Dawud. Thus the distances between the two kinds of Allah's creatures disappeared, and both creations were linked with the reality that had kept these veils between them, and both began to glorify and praise Allah, and their melody became one. This is a degree of harmony, purity and sincerity, and no one can reach this station and degree except by the grace of Allah. When the veils of the essential nature are lifted, Allah's creation becomes one, and all intervening veils are removed; no barrier remains. When Dawud (peace be upon him) sang the praise of Allah, the mountains and the birds sang along with him. The melody that was in the personality of Dawud (peace be upon him) would spread throughout the whole universe, and thus the whole universe would turn towards the Creator and sing His praise. This is that ... which is relished by those who have passed through such experiences and who have found such moments in their lives.

Wa alanna lahu al-hadeed (34:10): "And We made iron soft for him." This was another colour of Allah's grace that came upon Dawud (peace be upon him). From the manner in which the bounties upon Dawud (peace be upon him) are described here, it appears that this was an act beyond the ordinary course of nature. The matter was not like heating iron in furnaces to melt it and then working it by casting. Rather, it was a miraculous act and a proof of the prophethood of Dawud (peace be upon him), and the context of the discourse indicates this, since a particular grace is being mentioned here. It was not an ordinary and habitual technology.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 34, verse 11:

﴿أَنِ اعْمَلْ سَابِغَاتٍ وَقَدِّرْ فِي السَّرْدِ﴾ (34:11). "Sabighat" means coats of mail (zirah). It is said that before Prophet Dawud (عليه السلام), plates were made, and the coats of mail made of plates were heavy on the body and used to wound it. Allah taught Prophet Dawud (عليه السلام) this matter: that he should make them from hot wires so that they would be soft and the body could move within them like a garment. He was commanded to make the rings of this armour tight, so that arrows would not pass through them, and that all the rings should be made to a measured proportion. All of this work was done by inspiration from Allah. Further instructions were given to them in this way:

﴿وَاعْمَلُوا صَالِحًا ۖ إِنِّي بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾ (34:11). This is not only for the work of making armour, but in every work: do righteous deeds, and regard Allah as present in every matter. And believe that Allah is the Rewarder; nothing will remain hidden from Him. He is the All-Seeing of everything. This was the matter of Prophet Dawud (عليه السلام). As for Prophet Sulayman, a very great grace and favour was also bestowed upon him.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verse 12:

ولسلیمن الریح غدوھا شھر۔۔۔۔۔۔ وقلیل من عبادی الشکور (12 – 13) "They made for him whatever he wished: lofty buildings, images, and basins like reservoirs, and cooking pots fixed firmly in place. O family of Dawud, act in gratitude. Few of My servants are truly grateful."

For Sulayman (peace be upon him) the wind was subjected, and many narrations have been reported about it. A color of Isra'iliyyat (Israelite narratives) dominates these narrations, although they are not mentioned in the Jewish books. It is best to avoid getting caught up in these narrations. What the verse states is that Allah subjected the wind to Sulayman (peace be upon him), and this wind would blow in the morning toward one region (Sura al-Anbiya mentions that it blew toward the Holy Land), covering a distance of one month's journey, and in the evening it would blow toward another region, covering a distance of one month's journey. Sulayman would benefit from both, taking his advantages and making use of Allah's command. What the details of this are, we do not know, and there is no need to pursue people's accounts without verification.

واسلنا لہ عین القطر (34: 12) "We caused a spring of molten copper to flow for him." Qitr means copper, that is, brass. From the context here too it appears that, like the softening of iron, the spring of copper was also a miraculous act. It may be that Allah caused a copper spring to flow for them in the manner of a volcanic process, or that Allah taught them, by way of inspiration, how to melt copper. This too was a great favor from Allah.

ومن الجن من یعمل بین یدیہ باذن ربہ (34: 12) "And among the jinn were those who worked before him by the permission of his Lord." Allah miraculously subjected the jinn to him, and they performed miraculous duties in his kingdom. In Arabic, all those hidden powers that are not visible are called jinn. This is a creation to which Allah has applied the word jinn; we know about this creation only what Allah has told us, and no more. Here Allah has only said that a group of them was subjected to Sulayman (peace be upon him), who worked under his direction, and whoever among them fled, Allah would inflict a severe punishment upon him.

ومن یزغ ۔۔۔۔۔ عذاب السعیر (34: 12) Before the discussion of the subjection of the jinn was finished, a remark was made that the jinn are so under Allah's control that, if they disobey, Allah will cast them into the Fire. Since some polytheists worshipped the jinn, their helplessness is described here: just as the polytheists, their deities too will enter the Fire of Hell because of disobedience. In this way the jinn were subjected for Sulayman.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verse 13:

They made for him whatever he wished: [places of worship] (mahariib), statues (tamaatheel), basins like reservoirs (jifaan), and great cauldrons fixed firmly in place... (34:13). Mahareeb are the places where worship is performed. Tamaatheel refers to images made of brass and wood. Jifaan is the plural of jabiyah, a basin into which water flows. They used to make for Sulayman (peace be upon him) large bowls like reservoirs, and large cauldrons which stayed fixed in place because of their size. All these services were performed by the jinn. All these matters were extraordinary, beyond the normal course of things, so this is the correct interpretation of them. If they are reduced to the ordinary, then they are no longer a favour.

Now the address turns to the family of Dawud: "Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude" (34:13). We have provided this favour and bounty for you in the form of Dawud and Sulayman, so O family of Dawud, adopt the way of gratitude. Do not adopt the way of pride and boasting, but adopt the way of righteous action.

"And few of My servants are grateful" (34:13). This is a comment which places before the readers the reality of the matter, and it applies to all the stories of the Qur'an. The purpose is to show that Allah's favour and bounty upon mankind is so great that few people can give thanks for it, and human beings always fall short in performing the gratitude due to God. However much they give thanks, they still fall short. But if they do not give thanks at all, their fault will be very great. And if they rebel... The servants of Allah have very limited power, and they are not able to render thanks for the unlimited blessings of Allah. If someone were to count the blessings of Allah, they would not be able to count them. These blessings cover a person from above, a person is drowned in them from beneath his feet, and from the right, left, front and back a person enjoys them. His very being is immersed in them. He himself is an example of the blessings of Allah.

Once we were sitting, conversing with one another with great interest. All kinds of things were being discussed. Suddenly a small cat appeared, moving about us as though searching for something, but it was unable to say anything with its tongue. Suddenly Allah placed in our hearts that perhaps it was thirsty. When we provided water, it became clear that it was thirsty; it had intense thirst but could not express it with its tongue. At that moment we realised that among the favours and bounties of Allah upon man is a great favour: the tongue, the gratitude for which is not possible for man.

For a long time we had not seen the sun. The rays of the sun shone upon us only the size of a coin. We would stand before it and bring our mouths, hands and faces before the sun, and bathe our heads, backs and feet in the disc of its rays, and all of us did this action in turn. This was a blessing being given to us, and when on the first day we went out in the sunlight, I cannot forget that joy. No one can imagine the happiness that was on everyone's face at that time. Everyone was giving deep thanks to Allah and saying: "Alhamdulillah, this is the sun, and it has always been shining."

Daily these rays spread out, and we receive warmth from them and bathe in them. Thus we declare the purity of Allah and remain immersed in the blessing of Allah. Just consider how much benefit we derive from this great bounty of Allah which has been provided to us free and without reckoning, without hardship and without any difficulty.

If we were to go on presenting the blessings of Allah in this manner, our lives would come to an end, all our strength would be spent, and yet we would still be unable to count any considerable part of those blessings. Therefore we too here will be content with the same brief indication that the Qur'an has given, so that those of insight and reflection can think further for themselves and take from it as much as Allah wills. This is a portion of the blessings of Allah, and only the person who turns to it with the utmost attention, sincerity and single-mindedness can attain them.

Now we come to the final verses of the Qur'anic story. These are part of the final scene. Sulayman dies, and the jinn were still engaged in carrying out the commands which he had given during his life. The jinn did not know that Sulayman had died. Sulayman was standing leaning on his staff before the jinn when a termite ate away his staff and he fell down. Then the jinn came to know that because of their ignorance they had remained in that hardship.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 34, verse 14:

When We decreed death for him... in the humiliating punishment (13)

It is narrated that when the time of death of Hazrat Sulayman (peace be upon him) came, he was leaning on his staff. The jinn were carrying out their respective duties, and they had many severe tasks that they performed. For a long time the jinn did not know that Hazrat Sulayman had died, until a woodworm (ghun) gnawed at his staff. This insect, wherever it is, eats away badly at the roof beams, doors and pillars. In the Port Said area, people build houses and, fearing this woodworm, do not use a single piece of wood in them, because this insect devours every kind of wood. When it had gnawed through the staff, it could not bear Hazrat Sulayman, and he fell to the ground. Then the jinn came to know that Hazrat had already passed away. It was only here that the jinn came to know.

So when it became clear to the jinn... (34:14), "It became clear that had they known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment." These are the jinn whom the Arabs worship, and Allah made them subject to one of His servants, and they did not even have knowledge of the unseen that was close to them. Yet some people are so lacking in understanding that they ask them about distant matters.

The story of the household of Hazrat Dawud (peace be upon him) was the story of the believers who were deeply grateful for Allah's favour and bounty. In contrast to this is the story of the people of Saba. In Surah an-Naml, the circumstances of Hazrat Sulayman and the Queen of Saba have passed. Now their story relates to later periods, because the events mentioned here belong to the period after that. The more correct view is that when the people of Saba became rebellious, Allah took away His blessings from them, and after this these people were scattered from that region. In the time of Hazrat Sulayman (peace be upon him), these people were the owners of a very great and developed kingdom, and throughout their land there was prosperity and public welfare works. This is because the hoopoe (hudhud) presented this report before Sulayman (peace be upon him).

"Indeed I found a woman ruling over them, and she has been given everything, and she has a mighty throne. I found that she and her people worship the sun, instead of Allah." After this, the Queen of Saba again comes and becomes Muslim before Sulayman (peace be upon him). Therefore, the events here relate to the period after the time of the Queen of Saba. These calamities came upon them when they adopted rebellion, and because of their ingratitude to Allah, Allah took away His blessings from them.

The story begins with a description of the state in which they were: good days, abundance, progress, Allah's blessings, and every kind of produce, the demand of which was that they should have given thanks to Allah in return for these favours.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verse 15:

Lagad kana li-Saba... wa Rabbun Ghafur (15)

Saba is the name of the people who lived in southern Yemen. Their land was lush and green. A part of it remains in the same condition even today. They were so advanced that they had built a reservoir for the rainwater that came from the east and the south. They had constructed a dam with natural mountains on both of its sides. At the narrow place between the mountains they had built the dam, from which springs and canals flowed. They would close and open its water as needed. They had gathered a very large quantity of water and had control over the reservoir. Thus it was a vast means of irrigation for them. The people called it the Dam of Marib (Sadd Ma'rib).

The gardens were under the canals on the right and left sides of this dam. That is, the whole region was green and flourishing, beautiful and lovely, and this was a sign of the bounty of the Generous Lord. They were commanded to give thanks to the Forgiving Lord for these blessings.

Kulu min rizqi Rabbikum washkuru lahu (34:15): "Eat of the provision of your Lord and give thanks to Him." They were advised to reflect on the blessings of Allah, who gave them this beautiful land, provided every kind of produce in it, and then also forgave the shortcomings that had occurred from them.

Baldatun tayyibatun wa Rabbun Ghafur (34:15): "A goodly land and a Lord who is Forgiving." The land was excellent, fertile, full of blessings and ease, and the Lord was forgiving of the kingdom of the heavens. The question is: when the land yields every kind of fruit, and Allah is Ghafur and Rahim, then what is the justification for not giving thanks and not praising Allah? Yet, despite this, they did not give thanks.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verse 16:

﴿فَأَعْرَضُوا فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَيْلَ الْعَرِمِ وَبَدَّلْنَاهُم بِجَنَّتَيْهِمْ جَنَّتَيْنِ ذَوَاتَيْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ وَأَثْلٍ وَشَيْءٍ مِّن سِدْرٍ قَلِيلٍ﴾ (16)

They turned away from gratitude to Allah. They abandoned doing righteous deeds and began to misuse the blessings of Allah. Therefore Allah took away from them the prosperity in which they were living. He sent upon them such a severe flood that it swept away even the rocks that lay in its path. Al-Arim means rocks. Thus the dam broke. The water took the form of a torrent. These villages and gardens were destroyed, and they were unable to arrange again for the storage of water. Therefore drought took the place of prosperity. The land dried up and was scorched, the green gardens turned into thickets of wild jujube bushes, and the green land turned into desert.

﴿وَبَدَّلْنَاهُم بِجَنَّتَيْهِمْ جَنَّتَيْنِ ذَوَاتَيْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ وَأَثْلٍ وَشَيْءٍ مِّن سِدْرٍ قَلِيلٍ﴾ (34:16) "And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk and a few lote-trees."

Khamt (خمط) refers to the arak tree. Every thorny tree is also called khamt. Athl (اثل) is a tree that resembles the tamarisk (al-Tarfa'), that is, tamarisk. Sidr (سدر) refers to the lote-tree (jujube, بیری), and this lote-tree, which had by then become their best fruit, was also in small quantity.

Thus We recompensed them for their ingratitude. Are We not to punish any but the ungrateful? (34:17)... That is, they were given this punishment because of their ingratitude to the blessings of God.

Prosperity and comfort had been replaced by hardship and economic difficulties. Yet they had not yet been torn into pieces and scattered throughout the earth. Communication still existed between their towns and the blessed towns of Makkah al-Mukarramah and Bayt al-Maqdis. The region of Yemen, to the north of the land of Saba, was also inhabited, and through Makkah and Madinah, Yemen was connected to Syria and Bayt al-Maqdis. This route remained safe and open.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verses 20–21:

﴿And Iblis indeed found his assumption about them to be true, so they followed him, except for a party of the believers.﴾ (34:20)

﴿And he had no authority over them, except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from who is in doubt about it. And your Lord is Guardian over all things.﴾ (34:21)

Why did this people end up in such a fate on this path? Because Iblis found his scheme to be correct, and he succeeded in misguiding them. Yes, he could not mislead the people of faith; he could not mislead the group of believers.

For in every misguided society there remains a small number of people who refuse to be misguided, and this small group of believers is a witness that the truth remains firmly established in its place. Only one thing is needed: that someone seeks the truth. If someone seeks, the truth is found. Even in the worst circumstances, the truth remains established.

As for Iblis, he has no tyrannical authority over people such that he compels them and leads them to misguidance. Satan is imposed upon people in every state. Now, some among the people remain steadfast upon the truth, and some people do not seek the truth at all; they go astray. Then in the reality of the world it becomes evident who the believer is, and his faith saves the believer from the evil path.

﴿Except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from who is in doubt about it.﴾ (34:21) "From the one who is in doubt about the Hereafter." The person who believes in the Hereafter is saved, and the one who doubts about the Hereafter falls prey to Satan's misguidance. God already knows beforehand who will take the straight path and who will take the wrong one, but God issues His decrees only when they actually come into effect.

In this vast field, that is, in the vast field of God's planning and decree, Satan has been given the freedom to impose himself upon people without compelling anyone, and to bring out the results that were already in God's knowledge. In this field, the story of Saba is in reality the story of all the nations of the world. The narrative of the rise and fall of nations is the same as that of Saba. Therefore the scope of application of this verse is broadened; this principle is not confined to the people of Saba. The good and bad circumstances of all human beings come and go under this same principle. People's being guided or going astray occurs as a consequence of adopting the causes of guidance or the causes of misguidance.

﴿And your Lord is Guardian over all things.﴾ (34:21) Nothing is hidden from Him; nothing in the system of creation is purposeless or useless.

Lesson No. 192: At a Glance

This is a short lesson whose subject is tawhid (the oneness of God) and shirk (associating partners with God), yet in this lesson the human intellect is taken on a tour of the entire universe. Whether the cosmos is apparent or hidden, present or absent, of the earth or of the heavens, related to this world or to the Hereafter, during this journey a fear is cast over the human being to such an extent that his existence trembles, and the majesty of Allah overtakes him so completely that he becomes overwhelmed. Before the human being are placed the scenes of his lineage, his provision, and of reward and punishment. In this lesson, with extremely forceful words, the human being is shaken awake with the repeated word "Qul" (Say). In every sentence a matchless argument is brought forward, an argument of great strength.

Lesson No. 196: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 22 to 27

﴿Say: Call upon those whom you claim besides Allah.﴾ (34:22) This is a challenge set out across the vast field of the heavens and the earth.

﴿Say: Call upon those whom you claim besides Allah.﴾ (34:22) Say: call upon your deities whom you consider to be gods besides Allah. Call them, and let them come. Let them appear in the field, let them claim for themselves, or you claim on their behalf, what authority they have in the kingdom of the heavens and the earths. Nothing.

﴿They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth.﴾ (34:22) Clearly, neither they nor anyone on their behalf can make such a claim, for the owner is the one who has disposal over a thing, and they have no disposal over it. Therefore these deities own nothing, since they have no authority at all in this vast universe.

﴿And they have no share in either of them.﴾ (34:22) That is, they are neither the sole owners nor even co-owners of the heavens and the earth.

﴿And none of them is a supporter for Him.﴾ (34:22) That is, none of them is a helper of Allah.

A third possibility might be that they are voluntary helpers of Allah; this too is not the case. It appears that the reference here is to a particular kind of deities and a particular kind of shirk, namely the angels, whom the Arabs regarded as the daughters of Allah, considered intercessors, and about whom they made their statements.

﴿We worship them only that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position.﴾ (39:3) This is why the next verse negates intercession, in a scene that is extremely terrifying.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verse 23:

ولا تنفع ۔۔۔۔۔۔ اذن لہ "". Intercession with Allah will be made only by those to whom Allah grants permission. Allah does not grant permission to anyone who is not a believer and does not deserve intercession. Those who commit shirk do not remain deserving of it. Neither the angels have permission for it, nor others besides them, except those who will be granted permission for intercession. Under what circumstances will the intercessors intercede, despite having permission? How terrifying and how dreadful will they be?

حتی اذا فزع ۔۔۔۔۔ العلی الکبیر (23) "".

This is the scene of a day that will be extremely frightening. People will stand on the Day of Resurrection. Both the intercessors and those for whom intercession is being made will be utterly terrified. At first the intercessors will wait for permission. This waiting will be long. People will stand in anticipation and become tired. They will be frightened, their hearts will be fearful, and their ears will be listening for the verdict. When the decision is issued from the honoured presence of Allah, the intercessors and those for whom intercession is being made will be so frightened that they will not be able to comprehend the decision.

حتی اذا فزع عن قلوبھم (34: 23) "until, when the fear is removed from their hearts". When they come out of the state of dread, and the calamity that had left them stunned has passed, then they will say:

ماذا قال ربکم (34: 23) "What did your Lord say?" That is, they will ask one another. Perhaps some of them, having kept their senses, will have understood the matter.

قالوا الحق (34: 23) "They will say: The truth." Perhaps those who say this are the angels brought near to Allah, who spoke this concise and comprehensive statement, because whatever Allah says is certainly the truth. He is the truth, eternal truth and everlasting truth. Therefore His word is also truth.

وھوالعلی الکبیر (34: 23) "And He is the Most High, the Most Great." This attribute of Allah occurs in a place where the exalted majesty of Allah is manifest, and in such a place every person can perceive the loftiness of Allah's glory.

This concise surah is a sign that deep seriousness and fear pervade the atmosphere, so that even in it only a brief statement can be made. This is a terrifying occasion of intercession. What if it is not granted? And this is the state of the angels brought near. After this frightening scene, can anyone claim that He has a partner, or can any intelligent person hold such a belief?

This was the first blow upon the strings of reason and intellect. The second blow relates to the provisions that humans use by night and by day. Who provides these human necessities? If one reflects upon human life and the food by which it is sustained, this too is a proof and a clear evidence of the sole Being of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 34, verse 24:

قل من یرزقکم۔۔۔۔۔ اوفی ضلٰل مبین (24) ” “۔

Provision (rizq) is a real and living concern of every human being. Provision is the result of rain from the heavens, the light of the sun and its radiance. These matters were already known to those whom the Qur'an addressed. After that, many discoveries have been made and are still being made about provision. What are the provisions of the earth? Plants, animals, springs, rivers, minerals and treasures. People of earlier eras were also acquainted with these, and later people made further discoveries.

قل من یرزکم ۔۔۔۔۔ قل اللہ (34: 24) "Say: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?" Say: "Allah." Because they could not doubt this answer, nor could they claim any other answer apart from it. Say: provision is indeed given by Allah, and your affairs and their affairs are entrusted to Allah. One of you, surely, is upon misguidance. It is not possible that both are upon guidance, or both are upon misguidance. Therefore one party is upon one path and the other party is upon another.

وانا او ایاکم ۔۔۔۔۔ ضلل مبین (34: 24) "Indeed, either we or you are upon guidance, or are in clear error." This is an extremely moderate manner of speech in debate, in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) tells the polytheists that one of us and you is upon guidance and the other upon misguidance. The guided party and the misguided party are not specified, so that the listener may determine it himself after reflection, with great seriousness, without obstinacy, without argument, contention and wrangling. For the Prophet (ﷺ) was a guide and teacher; his aim was to show people the straight path, not to humiliate them by silencing them.

By this manner of speech, even the most hostile, arrogant, rebellious and aggressive person has his heart affected by the matter, and a person's rank and status is no obstacle to accepting the path of guidance. Even one who holds a lofty position submits and reflects with a very calm heart. He attains contentment. This manner of speech deserves deep consideration, especially from those who undertake the work of calling to Islam.

Now a third blow is struck upon the strings of reason and intellect, in a most just and equitable manner of speech. Every heart is brought to stand before its deeds and their consequences.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verse 25:

﴿Qul la tus'alūna ... ta'malūn﴾ (25)

The polytheists would accuse the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions of being wrongdoers, misguided and criminals, and of having abandoned the true religion of their forefathers. The people of falsehood have always called the people of truth misguided. This is the result of their fickleness and arrogance, and the answer to it is this:

﴿Qul la tus'alūna 'ammā ajramnā wa lā nus'alu 'ammā ta'malūn﴾ (34:25) "Say: You will not be questioned about the wrong we have done, nor shall we be questioned about what you do." Every person is responsible for his own deeds, and every person will receive only the recompense of his own deeds. Therefore it is each person's own task to think carefully before taking any step, towards success or towards destruction.

Thus the Qur'an shakes them up so that they reflect. The first stage on the path to truth is that a person reflects upon the way of truth. Now, the fourth strike:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verse 26:

﴿Say: "Our Lord will bring us together, then He will judge between us with truth. He is the Judge, the All-Knowing."﴾ (34:26)

In the previous lesson, Allah gave a combined judgment between the People of Truth and the People of Falsehood: of the two, only one is upon the truth, and the other is upon falsehood. The confrontation between truth and falsehood took place so that the People of Truth would turn toward the truth, the callers would present their call, and truth and falsehood would contend with one another. Doubts would be raised against proofs, and falsehood would try to throw truth down. But this state lasts only for a short time. After that, a decision is made between the two sides. This decision is decisive, and the one who decides it is a very great Ruler, and He is also All-Knowing. He decides on the basis of knowledge and recognition.

By describing Allah as "Fattah, 'Alim" (the Opener of Judgment, the All-Knowing), the purpose is to show that one can rely on Allah's judgment, because He is a Ruler who decides between truth and falsehood according to knowledge. He makes truth and falsehood clear and does not leave any confusion between them. The People of Truth and the People of Falsehood are not left mixed together, provided that truth presents its call with force, and applies its strength in this path. It should make full use of all its experience, and, exerting its full strength, entrust the matter to Allah, so that Allah, the Opener, the All-Knowing, may decide.

It is Allah's affair to determine when He decides between truth and falsehood, and the timing of that decision is also determined by Allah. There is no urge for haste in it, because it is Allah who brings truth and falsehood face to face, causes them to contend, and then causes a decision to be made. He is the Fattah, the Alim.

Now the final blow. This final blow resembles the first blow. In it, the so-called partners of Allah are challenged.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verse 27:

﴿Say: "Show me those whom you have joined with Him as partners. Nay, but He is Allah, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise."﴾ (34:27) "".

This is an extremely threatening and contemptuous question. Just show us, then, who these people are whom you have joined with Allah in divinity. Who are they? What is their standing? What rank do they hold? And what is their claim to occupy that position? Then, with the word "kalla" (no, never), they are rebuked: from where will they bring them, when Allah has no partner at all?

﴿Nay, but He is Allah, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.﴾ (34:27) Mighty and wise is none other than Allah. How could one whose attributes are these have a partner, and what need would He have of one? Therefore Allah has no partner. With this, this lesson concludes. At its end there are very decisive and instructive reflections, bearing in mind this vast universe, in circumstances where the stage of intercession on the Day of Judgment will come, in the context of the struggle between truth and falsehood, and in the context of contemplation and reflection within the human soul.

Lesson No. 197: A General Overview

This lesson presents the stance of the disbelievers toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Book revealed to him. It is the stance that the comfortable and well-off people have adopted against every messenger. People of this kind are deceived by their wealth, their children, and their social standing. Their concern is only with the benefits of this world, and they think that, since they surpass others in acquiring worldly gains, they are therefore the chosen and most excellent people, and that, because of this worldly wealth, they will be saved from the punishment of both this world and the Hereafter. Thus, the scene of what will happen to them in the Hereafter is set before them. This scene is presented as though it has already taken place, so that they may see that the things which have made them arrogant will be of no benefit to them on the Day of Resurrection. In this scene it is also shown that the angels and jinn whom they used to worship in the world will be of no benefit to them whatsoever on the Day of Resurrection. Within the dialogue of this scene, it is explained what weight carries value in the scale of Allah. In the same way, the false values which they hold close to their hearts in this world are automatically refuted. It is established that the expansion or restriction of provision depends on the will of Allah, and that it is not a proof of Allah's wrath or His pleasure; rather, it is a kind of trial.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verses 31–33:

وقال الذین کفروا۔۔۔۔۔ بین یدیہ ” “۔ This is the obstinacy in which the opponents of Islam were entangled from the very first day. They had decided that they would not accept guidance, even though its source lies in the earlier scriptures. They would neither believe in the Qur'an nor in any earlier Book. Neither in this, nor in the previous scriptures. This was the decision of the opponents of Islam in the past and it is the same today. The meaning is that they insist upon disbelief. They have firmly resolved that they will persist in disbelief and will not even reflect upon the proofs of guidance. Since they have already made this decision, the remedy for them is simply to present before them one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection.

ولو تری اذ ۔۔۔۔۔۔ الا ما کانوا یعملون (21 – 23)

This was their worldly position: "We will never believe in the Qur'an, nor will we accept any Book that came before it." But the condition of these wrongdoers on the Day of Resurrection will be worth seeing, when these people will stand before Allah and will be waiting as accused persons in the court of Allah for their punishment. At that time they will be certain that they had denied guidance, so the result is before them. Now nothing more will be in their power. They will curse and blame one another and will place the responsibility for this end upon each other. What will they say at that time?

یقول الذین ۔۔۔۔۔ انتم لکنا مومنین (34: 31) "Those who were held down in the world will say to those who considered themselves great: 'Had it not been for you, we would have been believers.'" At that time, in the terrifying situation they are in, they will place the responsibility upon the elders, because they can see that calamity is upon their heads. Today they speak this truth to their faces, but in the world they lacked the ability to speak this truth. Time, weakness and slavery did not allow them to speak the truth. They had sold the freedom that Allah had granted them. They had given up the honour that Allah had given to every human being. They had rendered inoperative the faculty of perception that was given to every person. Today all false and counterfeit values have perished. Before them is painful punishment. Now they speak this truth, but it brings them no benefit.

لو لا انتم لکنا مومنین (34: 31) "Had it not been for you, we would have been believers." And these elders also answer with great harshness and bitterness. The danger is now equal for both. They unnecessarily place their responsibility upon them. They too answer well.

قال الذین ۔۔۔۔۔۔ کنتم مجرمین (34: 32) "The great ones replied: Did we turn you away from the guidance that came to you? No, rather you yourselves were criminals." Thus they clearly refuse to accept any responsibility, and they admit that guidance had come. These arrogant ones in the world gave no importance to the weak at all. They did not seek their opinion, rather they did not even acknowledge their existence, and they could not bear that these weak people should oppose them or debate with them. But today, when punishment confronts them, they plainly deny, saying:

انحن صددنکم ۔۔۔۔۔ اذجآء کم (34: 32) "Did we turn you away when guidance came to you?" Rather, you yourselves were criminals. You had adopted a criminal course.

If this were the world, these weak people would have kept their lips sealed, but in the Hereafter all the false veils of the world will be lifted. False values will be destroyed. Eyes will be opened and hidden realities will come out from behind the veil. For this reason, these weak people too will speak openly there. Indeed, there they will speak face to face with the arrogant and will say that you alone are responsible for all this situation. You used to practise deceit night and day and used to prevent us from guidance. You held on to falsehood, imposed it upon us, and made the Islamic call suspicious in our eyes. You used your influence to mislead us.

وقال الذین استضعفوا ۔۔۔ ونجعل لہ اندادا (34: 33) Those oppressed people will say to those great ones: "No, rather it was the deceit of night and day, when you used to tell us to disbelieve in Allah and to make others equal to Him."

Now they come to know that this dialogue and contention is of no benefit to them, neither to the great nor to the lowly. Salvation is not possible for the great, nor for the small. Every group is guilty. However, the great bear the responsibility of their testimony and also the responsibility of misleading others. The small bear the responsibility of why they obeyed those great people. Being weak will not be a reason for pardon there. Allah had given them intellect and freedom. They did not use their intellect and sold their freedom of opinion. They agreed to remain parasites and accepted a life of humiliation. Therefore they became deserving of punishment. During this conversation, deep remorse overtook them and they began to conceal it, when they saw the punishment.

واسروا الندامۃ لما راوا العذاب (34: 33) "When they see the punishment, they will feel regret," and they will try to hide their remorse. This is a state in which what is in the heart remains in the heart. Tongues are silenced, lips are sealed, and severe punishment overtakes them.

وجعلنا الاغلل ۔۔۔۔۔ الذین کفروا (34: 33) "We shall place collars upon the necks of those who disbelieved." Now these people are bound in collars, but the direction of the matter turns away from them and it is said to ordinary evildoers: as you did, so you shall be repaid.

ھل یجزون الا ما کانوا یعملون (34: 33) "Will they be recompensed with anything other than what they used to do?" Now the scene of these wrongdoers, both the great and the small, comes to its close. Both are wrongdoers. The great are wrongdoers because they were rebellious and insolent and also misled others. The small are wrongdoers because they abandoned the dignity and freedom of the human station and became slaves of their fellow humans, submitting to humiliation before them. For both, there is an everlasting punishment.

The curtain falls, and the wrongdoers have seen their scene well; they are hard-pressed to live. They have seen every state of theirs, and they are alive upon this earth. Others too have seen this scene. Before everyone, there are still moments of respite. The words that the chiefs of Quraysh speak are the very words that the arrogant ones of earlier peoples also used to speak.

At times people imagine that goodness, truthfulness and purity always remain deprived.

Here the Qur'an separates worldly wealth, goods and provisions from the values that are exalted in the sight of Allah. It is decided that the restriction and abundance of provision are under Allah's will. This has no connection with Allah's pleasure and displeasure. At times Allah gives abundant provision to a person with whom He is displeased, and at times He gives it to one with whom He is pleased. At times it happens that both the people of evil and the people of goodness are poor and needy, but the causes and means are not the same in all circumstances.

At times Allah favours the people of evil more so that they advance further in rebellion, corruption and disobedience. Thus it is His purpose to seize them. They commit the greatest number of crimes so that they receive greater punishment. Then Allah punishes them in this world and will also punish them in the Hereafter. In accordance with His wisdom and planning, at times Allah restricts the provision of the people of evil, and then they commit further crimes. They despair of Allah's mercy, and because of their poverty they transgress the limits of mischief, wickedness, oppression and misguidance.

At times Allah showers provision upon the people of goodness so that they perform yet more good deeds. Had they no wealth, they would not be able to do these deeds, and also so that they give thanks to Allah: with the heart, with the tongue and with action. Through their wealth they earn good deeds which are stored for them with Allah. And at times the people of goodness are deprived so that their patience and gratitude in deprivation may be tested. It is seen how much they rely upon Allah, how much they hope for His mercy, how much they have certainty in Allah's decree, and how much they are content with His decree, and that the Lord, the Exalted, is good and everlasting. In this way their store for the Hereafter increases, and Allah becomes very pleased with them.

In any case, whatever the causes of abundance and restriction of provision may be, and whatever the reason relating to people's deeds and divine wisdom, the reality is that this matter is entirely separate from acceptance with Allah. On its basis there is no precedence or lag with Allah. Precedence and lag with Allah depend upon how the person who has been given abundance of wealth and children disposes of his wealth and children. Likewise, how much patience and gratitude the one who has been given restriction of provision shows. Therefore, if the person who has wealth and children disposes of his wealth and children well, Allah will increase his reward.

**Lesson No. 198: At a Glance**

The opening of this final lesson of the surah begins with the polytheists, their statements about the Prophet (ﷺ) and the noble Qur'an. They are reminded of the end that people like them have met. Reference is made to the stories of those nations in human history who were stronger, more knowledgeable and wealthier than they were, and who were seized in this very world.

Then, the strings of reason are struck continuously with the most severe blows. In the first blow, they are taught to think about Allah in solitude, removing all the obstacles and veils that prevent them from sound thought and insight. In the second blow, they are invited to consider the reality that the Prophet (ﷺ) is continuously giving this people a call from which he gains no benefit, and he does not ask them for any reward. So why do these people doubt the call of the Prophet (ﷺ) and turn away from it? After that, with "Qul, qul, qul" (Say, say, say), these blows are struck continuously, and they are so forceful that if any heart has even an atom's weight of consciousness, it cannot remain unaffected.

This lesson concludes with a very dynamic scene of the Day of Resurrection, which is itself highly vivid and suits the preceding blows.

**Lesson No. 198: Explanation of Verses**

**43 to 54**

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verses 44–45:

[Qur'anic verses 43–45 as cited in the Urdu text: "When Our clear verses are recited to them..." through "...then see how was My reprimand (nakir)."]

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would present before these people a perfectly clear truth, but they would counter it with the fables of the past. These were a few ancient customs and traditions, superstitions and myths, which they had clung to. Within them there was no coherence or connection either.

When these people saw that the Qur'an was presenting a simple and straightforward truth, and that its teachings constituted a complete and well-ordered system of life, reasonable and appealing to the heart, they sensed the danger that the myths, the unreasonable customs, handed down from their forefathers could not stand against this reasonable system of life. Therefore they declared that this new teaching was a threat to all their treasured customs.

﴿Indeed, this man only wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship﴾ (34:43). But merely levelling this accusation was not enough, because the mere claim that he prevents people from the gods of their forefathers could not be persuasive to everyone. Therefore, alongside it, they made another accusation: that the teachings which Hadrat Muhammad (ﷺ) presents are not from Allah.

﴿And they say, "This is nothing but a fabricated lie"﴾ (34:43). Ifk means lie and fabrication. The word muftari has been brought as emphasis, so that from the very beginning the value of the Qur'an is diminished, because once the true source of the Qur'an is made doubtful, its worth obviously decreases. And further, this accusation:

﴿And those who disbelieved said, regarding the truth when it came to them, "This is nothing but evident magic"﴾ (34:43). They made this accusation because the Qur'an was an extremely impactful speech; whoever heard it would find a tremor in their religious world. Therefore, saying merely that it is a lie and fabricated was not sufficient, so they offered an interpretation of its effect: that it is open magic. These were continuous accusations, one after another, and they were levelling these accusations against the Qur'an of Allah so that its effect would not reach people's hearts. But none of the accusations these people made had any proof on their side. They were all false accusations, meant to mislead the common people. Those who made these accusations were the chiefs and leaders. These chiefs and leaders themselves fully believed that the Qur'an is the true Book of God, that this Book is beyond human power, and that even the greatest speakers had become unable to produce speech of this kind. In Zilal al-Quran we have given several narrations of such people which show what their real opinion was about the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Qur'an, and we have also recorded the schemes they devised concerning the Qur'an and against it.

The Qur'an exposed this weakness of theirs, and said that these Arabs were unlettered; they were not People of the Book, so that they could make a decisive statement about the teachings of any heavenly Book. These people did not even know about revelation, so they were not experts on revelation either. Moreover, after Hadrat Isma'il (peace be upon him), no messenger had come to them, so that they could give an expert opinion on this matter. Therefore, whatever they say about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Qur'an and revelation, these are matters about which they have no knowledge.

﴿And We had not given them any scripture which they could study, nor had We sent to them before you any warner﴾ (34:44). Their hearts are made to feel: just consider the end of those who came before them and denied. You are far weaker in strength compared to those people. They had knowledge, they had wealth, they had power, and they were advanced; yet when they denied the messengers, the punishment of Allah overtook them and they were seized with a very severe grip.

﴿And those before them denied, and they had not attained one-tenth of what We had given them; yet they denied My messengers, so see how was My reprimand﴾ (34:45). The punishment of Allah was extremely destructive. Among these deniers there were some people about whom the Quraysh also had knowledge, so a reminder of them was sufficient for them. But here the question is posed in a mocking manner.

﴿So see how was My reprimand﴾ (34:45). Since the addressees knew what that punishment was, this interrogative style is extremely effective.

These people are invited with great seriousness: seek the truth with sincerity, try to understand the false propaganda that is being spread against the truth, and think about the call that is being presented to you, free from external influences, and determine its worth.
