Say, "I advise you of only one thing: that you stand up for Allah, in pairs and individually, and then reflect: there is no madness in your companion. He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment."

That is, reflect before Allah. And let this reflection be made by setting aside your personal desires, disregarding your own interests, and looking past the situations and inclinations of the world and the doubts and misgivings that arise in hearts. All these things distance a person from Allah. In short, set aside the established notions of your society and your community, and reflect upon the matter of Allah.

That is, take the message of the Islamic call in a simple manner, not in light of your prevailing notions. Do not take it in a purely logical and philosophical manner, in which there is much rhetoric but no real effort to know the plain truth. They are invited to adopt the serious path of natural thought instead of logic-chopping, one in which there is little clamour, no confusion of issues, no crookedness in thinking, and no murkiness in understanding, but rather clear and transparent thought.

Yet the search for truth in a natural manner is indeed the search for truth itself, since it is the straightforward way of thinking, upon which the prevailing ideas of society do not exert influence, nor do the wrong customs and traditions prevalent in society have an effect. Only the fear of God and the watchfulness of Allah are truly effective. The path of this thinking is only one: the path of God, the path of bowing before God, the path of God's pleasure. It is a selfless path in which no personal desire, no interest, and no gain has any influence; a purely natural thinking upon which no external factors exert influence. That is, thinking for Allah alone.

"Stand up for Allah, in pairs and individually" (34:46): that is, deliberate with one another on the matter of the Islamic call, in pairs, meaning consult together in a limited number, apart from clamour, separated from the crowd of the common people, without being influenced by circumstances and the masses, because common people are gradually swayed by temporary circumstances; and reflect alone, which is the most effective method of thought.

"Then reflect: there is no madness in your companion" (34:46): consider what there is in your companion that could be madness. Before you he speaks of intellect, reflection, and great wisdom. What is the matter he speaks of that would show any deficiency in his intellect? He speaks of matters that are firm, strong, and clear.

"He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment" (34:46): the possibility of the occurrence of a most severe punishment moves a person to reflect, and the warner has also given notice so that whoever wishes to be saved may be saved. It is like a man who shouts that a fire has broken out, so flee. If someone does not flee, he endangers himself, while the one calling out is a truthful person of the finest character.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abu Nu'aym Shayr, from Abdullah ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: One day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us and called out three times, "O people, do you know what my example and your example is?" The people said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He (ﷺ) said: "My example and your example is like a people who feared an enemy's attack. They sent a man to find out the situation and report. This man saw that the enemy had arrived. He began to shout, fearing that the enemy would seize him before his voice reached the people, so he waved a cloth from afar: O people, the enemy has come, the enemy has come, O people, you have been attacked!"

In another narration from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) it is reported: "I and the Hour have been sent together, and it is possible that the Hour may come before me."

This was the first blow. Now observe the second blow.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verse 47:

Qul ma sa'altukum... kulli shay'in shahid (47). First, you invited them to reflect, alone or in pairs, upon the Islamic movement: what is there in the call of your companion that could be the cause of madness (junoon)? Here it is said: what is the reason that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is so engrossed in warning the people and is warning them of a severe punishment? What, after all, is his benefit in this? What are its causes? What benefit does the Messenger (ﷺ) gain? The thinking and the power of reasoning of these people are directed, in a most effective manner, toward this reality.

﴿Say: "Whatever reward I have asked of you, let it be for yourselves."﴾ (34:47) This is a highly sarcastic manner of speech, and it also contains a rebuke for them. May this reward be blessed for you.

﴿My reward is only with Allah.﴾ (34:47) He is the one who has assigned me to this task. He alone will give the recompense. I hope from Him alone, and for the one who hopes for the gift of Allah, every gift of the people of the world becomes insignificant and worthless in his sight. Such a person does not even think about it.

﴿And He is, over all things, Witness.﴾ (34:47) He knows, He sees, and nothing is hidden from Him. He is a witness over me: whatever I think, whatever I say, and whatever I do. Now, the third plectrum:

Say: "Indeed, my Lord hurls the truth; He is the Knower of the unseen."

That is, what I have brought is the truth. It is a solid truth which Allah hurls with force. Who can stand against a truth that Allah is sending down with such might? This is an extremely vivid and graphic mode of expression. It is as though shells of truth are raining down, a bombardment is underway, and no one has the courage to stand before it. Allah is hurling shells of truth, He who is the Knower of the unseen. He hurls these shells with knowledge; with knowledge He directs them toward whoever He wills. His aim never misses. Nothing is hidden from Him, and nothing can escape the reach of this truth, because there is no barrier standing in its way. Before Allah, the target lies open.

The final blow: "Say: The truth has come, and falsehood can neither originate anything nor bring it back" (34:49).

The truth has come, the Messenger has come, the Quran has come, and the Islamic system of life has come plainly and directly. Make the announcement, and make it an open proclamation, that the truth has now arrived. This cannonball has been hurled with force; it has come with strength and with dignity.

"Falsehood can neither originate anything nor bring it back" (34:49). Falsehood has no beginning and no end. Its affair is now finished; its life is over; there is no field of action left for it. Its departure has been decided. This is a blow that shakes to the core. Whoever hears this proclamation becomes certain that there is no longer any room for falsehood to remain, and therefore no one but the truth shall rule from now on.

And indeed this is the reality: since the Quran came, the path of truth has been established in the world, and falsehood stands in a defensive position before this truth, because truth has firmly resolved to prevail. Although at times falsehood has material power, it has never been able to achieve ideological superiority over the truth. It is another matter that at times the people of falsehood overcome the people of truth, but this is a temporary shaking caused by the mistakes of the people of truth. As for the truth itself, it remains firmly in its place; it is clear, it is manifest.

And the final blow.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 34, verse 50:

Qul in ḍalaltu... Samīʿun Qarīb (50)

"If I go astray, its harm will fall only on me. I alone shall bear responsibility for it. And if I am guided, it is because of what my Lord reveals to me through revelation (waḥy). I am not authorized to do anything on my own initiative. I myself am only a follower of the signal (ishārah) I receive."

﴿Indahu samīʿun qarīb﴾ (34:50): "He hears all things and He is near." These people found Allah near. The attributes of Allah were seated in their imagination, and those attributes were effective in their actual lives. They were certain that Allah is All-Hearing and near, and that He observes their affairs directly. Their complaints and their counsels are all before Allah. Allah has not left His servants alone, nor handed them over to anyone else. Thus their lives passed in Allah's intimacy and love; they lived under His shelter, in His neighbourhood, within His kindnesses, under His watch. And this belief they found alive within their own souls, alive and in simple form. These attributes were not mere imagination; they were living and practical. ﴿Indahu samīʿun qarīb﴾ (34:50)

Now the surah concludes with one of the scenes of the Day of Judgment. This scene is full of movement and rushing about.
